messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: The cited text describes three FF configurations (one-stage 20% foam fraction, one-stage 1%, three-stage 1%), all treating PFAS-contaminated landfill leachate with a common functional unit of 1000 m3 and a shared system boundary up to foam waste disposal. This supports the judgment that the scenarios are quantitatively comparable with conditions.

The endpoint is life-cycle global warming potential, a modeled impact metric rather than a direct PFAS concentration or removal endpoint. Classifying it as 'other' is appropriate and consistent with the abstract’s description of LCA-derived GWP (818 kg CO2 eq).

The second endpoint summarizes multiple LCA impact categories (e.g., ecotoxicity, ozone depletion) as shown in the results table. These are also modeled impact metrics, so classification as 'other' is appropriate.
Both the abstract and results specify that the study treats PFAS-contaminated landfill leachate, matching the matrix description.
The text explicitly states a functional unit of treating 1000 m3 of PFAS-contaminated landfill leachate, matching the recorded value description.
The functional unit is defined per 1000 m3 treated; using 'm3 treated' as the unit is consistent with the source description.
The results section clearly refers to a 'one-stage FF system' with a single vessel, supporting the system configuration description.
The text states that the foam '20% or 1% volume of the input LL' is extracted, supporting a 20% foam fraction scenario.
The source describes the foam as a percentage of input landfill leachate volume; the unit '% of input landfill leachate volume' correctly reflects this.
The foam is described as being sent to 'the disposal unit, which is hazardous waste incineration,' matching the foamate management description.
The results section notes that 'Compressed air flows from the bottom,' which matches the described aeration mode.

Multiple sections refer to PFASs in landfill leachate without giving a detailed compound-by-compound profile in the cited chunks, supporting the description of a PFAS mixture without resolved chain-length composition in this context.
The abstract reports that the global warming potential was estimated at 818 kg CO2 eq for the one-stage system with 20% foam fraction; the value 818 matches exactly.
Given the functional unit of 1000 m3 treated and the reported GWP in kg CO2 eq, the unit 'kg CO2 eq per 1000 m3 landfill leachate treated' is consistent with the source.
The conclusion states that the conventional one-stage FF with 20% foam fraction has a large volume of hazardous foam waste of 200 m3 per 1000 m3 treated; the value 200 is correctly transcribed.
The source explicitly gives '200 m3 per 1000 m3 treated,' matching the unit 'm3 foam waste per 1000 m3 landfill leachate treated' in the record.
The text specifies the foam volume as '20% or 1% volume of the input LL'; 20% is correctly captured as a numeric value of 20.
The foam fraction is described as a percentage of the input landfill leachate volume; the unit '% of input landfill leachate volume' accurately reflects this.

The results section clearly states that the study evaluates burdens up to disposal of foam waste and that 'the impact of downstream effluent quality is excluded from the system boundary,' matching the reported limitation.

The abstract and results specify PFAS-contaminated landfill leachate and particular FF configurations (e.g., one-stage with 20% foam fraction). It is a valid design-inferred limitation that results may not generalize beyond this matrix and configuration.

The text states that foam is sent to hazardous waste incineration but provides no data on PFAS destruction or residual PFAS post-incineration in the cited chunks; inferring this as a limitation on quantified residuals is reasonable and supported by design.

The abstract describes a parametrized LCA and LCCA using full-scale operational data and EPA design models, indicating a system-scale, full-scale design basis model, consistent with the recorded description.

The results section describes a one-stage FF system where compressed air is introduced from the bottom, foam is extracted (20% or 1% of input LL), and foam is sent to hazardous waste incineration, matching the recorded treatment description.

result.record_usable_rationale: All core elements of the record—including source identity, matrix, treatment configuration, functional unit, foam fraction, foam waste handling, and key quantitative findings—are directly supported by the cited text with correct numeric values and units. No contradictions or major omissions that would mislead synthesis are present, so the record is usable.
